A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MM-Mem and contain readable text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–F. Corresponding content can be matched despite pagination and numbering changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original MM-Mem benchmark results, component ablations, memory visualizations, and SFT versus reinforcement-learning comparisons, including Appendix F.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds measurements of memory use, construction time, and inference latency.

M1.justification: Section 3.1 replaces separately stored visual/textual traces with an integrated-memory description and explicitly includes visual pointers in symbolic-memory records. However, v1 already defines paired multimodal entries and grounding edges, while update actions, SIB-GRPO, and retrieval rules remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish whether storage or computation changed beyond the description.

E1.justification: Both versions use Video-MME, MLVU, HD-EPIC++, and VStream-QA, including its Ego and Movie splits. The new efficiency study uses the existing Video-MME setting without subtitles and adds no distinct task or input scenario.

E2.justification: New efficiency Table 4 includes VideoAgent, absent from v1's reported comparisons, alongside existing comparators Qwen3-VL-8B, Video-RAG, and Vgent. Comparator membership in the retained accuracy tables and appendix experiments is unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 4.4 adds an efficiency protocol covering Video-MME's three length regimes without subtitles, measuring peak VRAM and construction/inference times normalized per minute of video. Existing data splits, training settings, accuracy metrics, and automatic judging protocols are unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds an efficiency and deployment analysis examining construction cost, inference latency, and GPU memory requirements. Existing component ablations, memory-topology visualizations, qualitative examples, and Appendix F analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Appendix F.2 retains the same repeated-evaluation uncertainty description and identical mean-plus/minus values. No new run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty estimates for the efficiency measurements are reported.

E6.justification: New Table 4 reports MM-Mem at 17.8 GB peak VRAM, 19.54 seconds construction time, and 5.35 seconds inference time per video minute; Vgent reports 18.7 GB, 20.18 seconds, and 7.38 seconds. These are newly reported measurements. Accuracy results in Tables 1–3 and Appendix F are unchanged.

T1.justification: The IB assumptions, variational bounds, optimization equations, entropy criterion, and Appendix A proofs are unchanged apart from numbering. Section 3.1 makes the existing grounding-edge neighbors explicit as pointer sets in the symbolic-memory notation, without adding a mathematical argument or formal property.

C1.justification: The introduction qualifies the central Fuzzy-Trace Theory analogy as cross-modal fusion with predominantly visual/verbatim and textual/gist roles, replacing the more direct alignment framing. The principal contributions remain unchanged. The abstract's state-of-the-art wording repeats a claim already present in v1's introduction and conclusion.

C2.justification: Sections 3.1–3.2 add explanations of changing modality dominance, sensory text as a visual label, and grounding links as multimodal pointers. Section 4.5 adds an interpretation of construction costs being amortized across queries. The limitations and Appendix F's weaker Movie-split findings remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents peak memory requirements and separate construction/inference costs, and explains unavailable efficiency measurements. The A100 platform, backbone, retrieval models, training and inference hyperparameters, prompts, and repository access information are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to LicoMemory, VideoAgent, and the work on inducing high energy-latency with verbose images. It includes LicoMemory among text-centric agent memories and VideoAgent among long-video approaches. The broader research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: There are targeted rewrites in the introduction, related work, memory description, and qualitative discussion, plus a new efficiency subsection and acknowledgments. Affiliations and publication information are updated. The overall narrative order and appendix organization are retained.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is redrawn with visual/textual artifacts at each memory level, revised labels, and a logo. Efficiency Table 4 is added, and existing displays are repositioned through reflow. The remaining figures and appendix displays retain their content.

improvement.justification: The new efficiency study supplies concrete evidence for previously qualitative deployment claims, and Section 3.1/Figure 2 explain grounding links more explicitly. These are useful, limited gains while the accuracy evidence and proofs remain stable. Sparse profiling details and ambiguity about whether the revised memory description reflects an implementation change limit the overall improvement.
